title: Intracranial entrainment reveals statistical learning across levels of abstraction (Sherman et al., 2023): raw iEEG from 8 neurosurgical patients
description: Raw intracranial EEG (iEEG) recorded from 8 neurosurgical patients with electrodes implanted for seizure monitoring. Patients viewed rapid streams of scene photographs containing statistical structure at either the category level or the exemplar level, alongside a random-order baseline. The data were used to test whether neural entrainment reveals statistical learning across levels of abstraction. This release is a BIDS conversion of the original Dryad data.
methods_description: Recordings used a Natus NeuroWorks EEG system sampled at 4096 Hz, with a reference electrode chosen by the clinical team to minimize noise. Scene images were shown for 250 ms each, followed by a 250 ms inter-stimulus interval, in category-structured, exemplar-structured, and random conditions. A custom DAQ inserted 8-bit triggers into an open EEG channel (TRIG). The EDF files are unprocessed apart from anonymization of the date information.
